solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dull tone largely set by company executive before drink

indicators.note: before places the executive ahead of the drink in the answer
largely means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a hue is a shade or tone of colour
MD is managing director, a company executive
rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: A musical note drags on, set to a boss's habit of drinking first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' trims HUE to HU; 'set by' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something monotonous and lacking excitement is described with this adjective, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Label carried by old gear providing security

indicators.note: carried by means the label sits inside the old gear

parts.note: hose is old-fashioned legwear, clothing or gear
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A name tag sewn into old clothing serves as a guarantee.
explanation.walkthrough: HOSE here is the old word for stockings or tights.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive held as a pledge guarantees a deal, a kind of security.

clue.text: Festivity with artist arising in US college associated with a cocktail

indicators.note: in places the reversed pieces inside the college

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

indicators.note: arising, in a down clue, means the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: a rag is a British student charity festivity
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A student party with an artist at an American college is linked to drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' turns RAGRA into ARGAR inside MIT, then A follows; 'associated with' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A tequila, lime and orange liqueur drink served in a salt-rimmed glass is a cocktail.

clue.text: What injured jockey did in stock venue?

definitions.text: What injured jockey did in stock venue?

parts.words: What injured jockey did in stock venue?
parts.note: a venue for cattle and horses where riders are thrown; the past tense of ride plus an 'oh' of pain

explanation.surface: A hurt rider recalls what happened at a livestock show.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads as 'rode, oh!', a cry from someone hurt in the ring of cowboy contests.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowboy contests of bronco riding and roping are staged at this livestock show.

clue.text: Low thing possibly to hoard pounds and work illegally

parts.note: to low is to moo, as a cow does

indicators.note: to hoard means the pounds are kept inside the rearranged word
possibly signals the word thing is to be rearranged

parts.note: L is pounds sterling, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A lowly figure stockpiles money and works off the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns THING into NIGHT, and 'to hoard' puts L after its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding a second job on the side, often undeclared to taxmen, is to moonlight.

clue.text: A German occupying limited store that's very awful?

indicators.note: occupying means the German article sits inside the shortened store
limited means the store word is cut short at its end

parts.note: to house goods is to store them; a house is also a store, as in a warehouse
ein is German for 'a'

explanation.surface: A German taking over a small shop is portrayed as the villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' and 'occupying' are the two indicators; 'that's' is a link, and the question mark softens 'very awful' as a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinous acts are wicked in the extreme, so dreadful beyond the ordinary, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Old TV cop that's hard and tough hiding head

parts.note: H is hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: hiding head means the first letter is concealed and dropped

parts.note: butch means tough and rugged

explanation.surface: A veteran TV detective is hard and rough and keeps his head down.
explanation.walkthrough: Hutch is one of the pair of detectives in the 1970s US show Starsky and Hutch.
explanation.definitionFit: Detective Ken Hutchinson from the 1970s police series is known by this nickname.

clue.text: Hot-headed manoeuvring of basic flier ignoring fighter plane

indicators.note: manoeuvring suggests the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: F is the designation for a US fighter plane, as in F-16

explanation.surface: An angry trainee pilot struggles with a fighter jet.
explanation.walkthrough: BASIC FLIER less F is rearranged to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone quick to anger, short-tempered, is described as hot-headed.

clue.text: Fruit all recorded presumably?

definitions.meaning: a small oval stone fruit grown on Mediterranean trees
read as '...', nothing live, so everything presumably pre-recorded

explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean stone fruit, and a jokey phrase 'O live' meaning nothing broadcast live.

clue.text: Military figures putting missile on old city road

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the missile above the city so it comes first

parts.note: SAM is surface-to-air missile
Ur is an ancient Mesopotamian city
the A1 is Britain's Great North Road, written AI

explanation.surface: Soldiers set a missile on an ancient city's road.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's longest numbered road; crosswords write it as AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese warrior caste members were military men, so these are military figures.

clue.text: Dispose of wine behind small hotel

indicators.note: behind puts the wine after the two letters

parts.note: H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet and on maps
red is wine, as in a glass of red

explanation.surface: Someone gets rid of the wine round the back of a little hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear documents into strips is a way to get rid of them for good.

clue.text: A storm is erupting about Catholic getting banishment

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters wrap around the Catholic letter
erupting suggests the words burst apart and are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A violent storm breaks out over a Catholic who is being sent into exile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erupting' turns A STORM IS into OSTRAISM, and 'about' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Athenians exiled citizens by vote; the word now means exclusion from society.

clue.text: Religious high-up returns greeting volunteers after a year

indicators.note: after puts the greeting and volunteers following A and the year letter
returns means the greeting and the volunteers together are read backwards

parts.note: hallo is a greeting, a variant of hello
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A senior cleric comes back to greet volunteers after a year away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns HALLOTA into ATOLLAH as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior Shia Muslim cleric holds this title, a high rank in religion.

clue.text: Applaud food

definitions.meaning: to applaud is to shout approval
good fare, as in the phrase 'good ...', meaning food and drink

explanation.walkthrough: The food sense is older, as in 'Christmas cheer' for a seasonal spread.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to shout encouragement; the noun once meant fare or provisions laid on.

clue.text: Throw out bunch blocking crime victims

indicators.note: a bunch of letters blocking the gap across the two words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Gangs block the way of crime victims and turn them out.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove a tenant from a property by legal process is to expel them.

clue.text: Expression of approval in ecstatic state for permissiveness

indicators.note: in places the approving shout inside the ecstatic state

parts.note: a trance is a dreamlike or ecstatic state
ole is the Spanish cheer of approval

explanation.surface: A shout of approval in a state of rapture reflects a liberal attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is willingness to allow behaviour one dislikes, which is permissiveness.

clue.text: One in outfit taken with supermarket biscuit

indicators.note: taken with joins the supermarket name on after
in places the numeral inside the outfit

parts.note: garb is clothing, an outfit
I is the Roman numeral for one
Aldi is a discount supermarket chain

explanation.surface: Someone in a uniform goes to the supermarket for a biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: A GARIBALDI is a British biscuit of currants pressed between thin layers of dough.
explanation.definitionFit: This currant-filled British biscuit, named after the Italian general, is a type of biscuit.

clue.text: Group with criminal to reserve funds?

parts.note: a ring is a group, often of criminals
a fence is a criminal who handles stolen goods

explanation.surface: A gang with a crook plans to stash away money.
explanation.definitionFit: To set money aside so it cannot be spent elsewhere is to protect it with a barrier.

clue.text: Weariness in boss not having succeeded in film

indicators.note: in places the shortened boss inside the film

parts.note: Lassie is a famous film about a collie dog

indicators.note: not having means the letter for succeeded is removed from the boss word

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised knob or ornament
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: An exhausted manager drops out of a film.
explanation.walkthrough: A boss is a raised knob or stud on a shield; 'not having' and 'in' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is lethargy and physical tiredness, the same state as weariness.

clue.text: Fake US city immersed in daily sun

indicators.note: immersed in means the city sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: a daily or char is a British cleaning lady who comes in each day
to sun oneself is to tan
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A Los Angeles figure soaks in the sun every day, a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' is British for a cleaner who comes in daily, also called a char.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack or impostor claiming false skills is a fraud, as is a fake person.

clue.text: Pay out with sign of illness on the increase?

parts.note: a cough is a symptom of illness
up means rising, on the increase

explanation.surface: Paying a bill gives someone a cough, and it is getting worse.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand over money reluctantly is a slang phrase for paying out.

clue.text: Poems analysed in course

indicators.note: analysed suggests the poems are broken down and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Poems are studied as part of a course of literature.
explanation.walkthrough: EPSOM is a racecourse in Surrey, home of the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: The Surrey racecourse where the Derby is run is a horse-racing course.

clue.text: Discern type in error

parts.note: a make is a type or brand
out means wrong, as in 'out in one's reckoning'

explanation.surface: Someone spots a mistake in the typesetting.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage to see or understand something is to perceive it, a phrasal verb.

clue.text: Monarch heading off having acquired cold sore

indicators.note: having acquired means the shortened monarch takes in the cold letter
heading off removes the first letter of the monarch word

parts.note: a monarch is a ruler
C is cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A king who loses his head after catching a cold gets a sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' trims RULER to ULER and 'having acquired' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An open lesion on skin or a membrane is a type of sore.

clue.text: Line with support, we hear, for smart girl

indicators.note: we hear signals the words are spoken and sound like the answer

parts.note: a queue is a line of people and a tee is a support for a golf ball

explanation.surface: A girl in a queue is propped up, apparently looking smart.
explanation.definitionFit: An attractive or clever young woman is informally called this endearment.

clue.text: Perhaps, cordial fellow, Irish politician, put in order timeless writing material

indicators.note: put in means the fellow and politician go inside the trimmed word
timeless means the T for time is removed

parts.note: to sort things is to order them
TD is Teachta Dala, a member of the Irish parliament
ink is a writing material

explanation.surface: A friendly Irish politician arranges his writing things.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the front, split by a comma; 'timeless' drops the T for time, and 'put in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordial is one example of a non-alcoholic beverage, as the word perhaps signals.

clue.text: Petty row about river fish

indicators.note: about means the petty row wraps around the river

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A small quarrel about a river and its fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A small herring-like sea fish caught around Europe is a fish.

clue.text: Charge one coming out on appeal

indicators.note: on joins the debutante word ahead of the appeal word

parts.note: a deb, debutante, is a young woman coming out into society
it is sex appeal

explanation.surface: A charge is laid on someone appealing their case.
explanation.walkthrough: A debutante 'comes out' into society; 'it' is old slang for sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry recording money owed in an account is a charge against it.

clue.text: Criminal activity associated with aggressive batsman?

definitions.meaning: driving off after causing an accident, an offence
a batsman in cricket who strikes hard and dashes between the wickets

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman scores runs by hitting the ball and running between the wickets.
explanation.definitionFit: The offence of leaving a crash scene, and literally a batsman who strikes and then sprints.

clue.text: Famous boxer, British one found in Italy

parts.note: uno is Italian for one

explanation.surface: A celebrated British fighter turns up in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank BRUNO is a British heavyweight boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Bruno, former world heavyweight champion, is a well-known British fighter.

clue.text: School authority in cheap refectory

indicators.note: in signals that the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A head boy keeps order in the cut-price school dining hall.
explanation.walkthrough: A PREFECT in a British school is a senior pupil given some authority.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior pupil with disciplinary duties in a British school holds authority there.

clue.text: Petition beginning to exercise northern doctor

indicators.note: beginning to means only the opening letter of exercise is used

parts.note: to doctor an illness is to treat it

explanation.surface: A northern doctor is asked to start a patient on exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To petition someone is to beg or plead earnestly, a verb synonym.
